body.statement: For every \(n\ge1\), \(\inf_{M_0\in M_G}\Pr_{M_0}\{\Theta(p_0)\subseteq I_{\mathrm{abs}}\}\ge1-\alpha\). Here \(p_0\) is the law of the fixed measurable finite code \(Z=\kappa(O)\), so \(\Theta(p_0)\) is the entire full-Lipschitz-class identified set induced by that code, not by the unbinned continuous observational law. Together with the two-sided lifting, this is the whole-set finite-sample component absent from both Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim's finite exact canonicalization and Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis's mixed-variable graphwise Wasserstein approximation; no model-class containment is asserted. The interval \(I_{\mathrm{abs}}\) is mathematical and need not be computable.
body.justification: Exact observable-law inversion and deterministic set inclusion deliver whole-set validity without endpoint differentiability or a computational encoding assumption.
body.gap: Romano and Shaikh provide uniform asymptotic identified-set coverage. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim's Definition 2.3 and Theorem 2.4 concern finite exact canonicalization. Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis define their estimator at finite sample and prove almost-sure asymptotic consistency and bracketing, but do not provide an exact finite-sample confidence region uniformly covering the whole fixed-coded-law identified set.
body.consumer: The theorem supplies the validity benchmark against which any implementable certified subclass can be assessed.
